title: Risotto alla Milanese
subtitle: Saffron risotto from Milan
excerpt: The Milanese classic: creamy risotto coloured deep gold by saffron, finished with a generous amount of butter and parmesan. Simple ingredients, precise technique.
sourceNotes: Milanese culinary tradition; saffron risotto has been a fixture of Lombard cooking since the sixteenth century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Risotto does not keep well. Make it and serve it immediately.

content.text: Risotto alla Milanese is golden, silky, and unmistakably Lombard. The saffron goes in early so the colour runs through every grain. Do not rush the stock additions; give each ladle time to be absorbed.

items.prepNote: kept hot in a separate pan
steeped in 4 tbsp of hot stock for 10 minutes

content.text: Steep the saffron in 4 tablespoons of hot stock. Set aside for at least 10 minutes. Keep the rest of the stock hot in a separate pan.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a wide, heavy pan over a medium heat. Add the shallots and a pinch of salt. Cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until every grain is coated and looks slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in the wine. Stir until fully absorbed. Add the saffron-infused stock and stir again.
Add the hot stock one ladle at a time. Stir and wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This will take 18 to 20 minutes.
When the rice is tender with a slight bite and the mixture moves in slow waves when you shake the pan, take it off the heat.
Add the remaining cold butter and the parmesan. Stir vigorously for 1 minute, then cover and rest for 2 minutes. Serve straight away.

items.symptom: The risotto is stiff and gluey.
items.cause: Too much stirring drove out too much starch, or it was left too long off the heat before serving.
items.fix: Beat in a small ladle of warm stock and serve immediately. Risotto should be eaten the moment it is ready.

items.symptom: The colour is pale, not golden.
items.cause: The saffron was not steeped long enough or too little was used.
items.fix: Use a generous pinch and allow at least 10 minutes of steeping. The colour deepens as it cooks.

items.symptom: The rice is chalky in the centre.
items.cause: Not enough stock was added or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Add more warm stock a ladle at a time and cook on a lower heat, giving each addition more time to absorb.
